symptom: A Data grid 2 an older mxcli stored with SortBar.SortItems marker 3 kept it through every `create or replace page`, including one that changed the page for real, while Studio Pro and a page created from nothing store 2. mx check, mx diff (names only, 0 changeDetails), lint and `fix property-sets` were all clean. Separately, a populated Forms$CallNanoflowClientAction / Forms$NanoflowSource ParameterMappings list was written with marker 3 where Studio Pro writes 2
cause: A marker registration only reaches lists the encoder builds. An unchanged pluggable widget's Type and Object pass through byte for byte (passStoredThrough), and the codec copies an existing element's clean properties as raw bytes, so a stored list keeps the marker an older build gave it. The nanoflow lists had no owner/key registration, and the child type (Forms$NanoflowParameterMapping) has no marker of its own, so a populated list took the default 3
fix: The marker tables moved to canon. Every write (normalizeForStorage, so insert, update and transaction alike) runs canon.NormalizeListMarkers, which gives each list with a registered owner/key marker that marker anywhere in the unit and leaves unregistered lists and child-type registrations alone. Registered the two nanoflow lists as 2
insight: `drop page` plus the same MDL giving 2 while the rewrite kept 3 points at pass-through, not at the writer: look for what the rewrite copies rather than what it builds. Applying a registration to stored bytes turns a wrong registration into a rewrite of Studio Pro's bytes, so the census (every owner/key registration against TestApp and PedApp, plus normalization as a fixed point on every fixture unit) is a test. A forced-wrong registration fails it twice: 164 disagreements and 114 changed units. Child-type markers are not applied: they are the encoder's rule for lists it builds, not a measurement of every list starting with that child. Do not fix this with `fix property-sets`: a stale marker breaks no merge or check, so the units nobody rewrites can keep it
